use_when: To list records people scan, compare and act on in the back office, such as rate seasons, admins, invites or documents.
Put the name of each record in the first column (primary), the status in a tag, and row actions such as "Edit" or "Resend · Revoke" in the last column.
Turn on the checkbox column when people act on several rows at once, and show the selected rows in light blue.

dont_use_when.when: On the guest website or app for browsing stays: use Card type listing.
For two or three facts about one thing, such as in a dialog: use detail rows.
Put long text or paragraphs in a cell: link to a detail page instead.

variant_intent.success: Live, On file (the success tag tone).

placement: Under header type=backoffice, to the right of the SideBar (the BackOfficePage story).

a11y.fact: A native <table> with an accessible name from tableLabel (default "Data table"), so a screen reader announces rows and columns.
Column headers are <th scope="col"> and the primary cell of each row is <th scope="row">, so each cell is read with its column and row name.
A sortable header is a native <button> and its <th> carries aria-sort (none, ascending or descending); the arrow is hidden from assistive technology.
The row and header checkboxes are Horizon's Checkbox, a native input, labelled "Select <row name>" and "Select all rows"; selection is the checked state, not colour alone.
Action cells are Horizon's Link, a native <a href>, and Previous / Next are Horizon's Button, native <button> elements that take the disabled attribute.
The footer summary is an aria-live="polite" region and Previous / Next sit in a <nav> named "Pagination".
A keyboard focus ring (color/border/focus, 2px) is drawn on the checkboxes, the sort button and the action links.
